summary.headline: Ksolves Q1 FY27 revenue rose 10% YoY to Rs 41.4 crore, but management withdrew FY27 revenue guidance while EBITDA margin hit 30.3%.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue for Q1 FY27 (quarter ended 30 June 2026) was Rs 41.4 crore, up 10% YoY but down 3.7% QoQ, as two long-standing large clients cut work and some engagement ramp-downs landed late in the quarter. EBITDA was Rs 12.56 crore (up 26.2% YoY, flat QoQ) with margin at 30.3%, and PAT was Rs 9.21 crore (up 43.3% YoY, down 5% QoQ). Management said it would not reaffirm FY27 revenue guidance, now expecting flat-to-4-5% growth at most, and reiterated a 25-30% EBITDA margin range. The company remains debt-free and declared an interim dividend of Rs 4 per share.

segments.name: Core IT services
segments.commentary: Contributed 98.3% of Q1 FY27 revenue; management now describes the company as fully services-focused, with product business not a focus.

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: 82% of revenue from overseas: North America 63%, India 18%, Europe 6%, Australia 3%, rest of world 10%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance not reaffirmed; management says FY27 revenue may be similar to FY26, with growth of up to 4-5% YoY if things go well.
EBITDA margin target maintained at 25-30% for full year and QoQ, with a move toward the upper end if revenue improves.
Softer revenue expected for the next two to three quarters as ramp-downs flow through; full impact seen over that period.
FY28 guidance to be revisited in March 2027.
Longer-term aspiration stated: about 20% growth after FY27 with roughly 30% margin, though management also said 'upper side of 30%' margins if things go well.
capex_capacity: Hiring is restricted to requirement basis; AI-driven productivity is cited as the lever to scale output with fewer new resources.
Developer efficiency reportedly up about 25% (four developers' work now done by about two); some senior developers reportedly up to 3x.
Management says the company will become an official Claude partner soon; all staff reportedly AI-certified and an enterprise Claude licence provided to everyone.
demand_pricing: Clients are tightening budgets and delaying decisions; two long-standing large T&M clients (3+ years) reduced work and headcount, citing a global headcount reduction, a management change at one, and losses at the other, not AI insourcing.
Management says most top-10 clients are stable or expanding; company added some new customers and revenue in the quarter.
Pipeline of about USD 1 million cited, with two deals of USD 300K and USD 250K; the rest undisclosed.
A major international bank (AI-hosted platform, principal vendor, roughly year-long project, still in discussion, more than 50 use cases) is in discussion; Salesforce is involved.
Middle East: no new business in the last quarter and none expected in the next few quarters; existing yearly contracts renewed. Focus shifted to Europe, Australia and the US.
More than 80% of revenue from repeat customers, per CFO.
Management says nearly every new proposal now asks for AI.

qa_highlights.question: Is the slowdown concentrated among a few large clients?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said most of the top 10 are stable or growing; two clients with 3+ year relationships cut work and headcount, with one expected to ramp up next year.

qa_highlights.question: Are the two clients moving AI in-house?
qa_highlights.answer: Management denied this, saying the cuts were business decisions (global headcount reduction, management change, losses) and that the clients had been heavily using Ksolves on AI work.

qa_highlights.question: Will the current year look like FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said revenue may be similar to FY26, with margins still improving and staying within 25-30%.

qa_highlights.question: Has AI improved efficiency and have token costs been factored into margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Developer efficiency is about 25% (senior developers up to 3x); management said token costs are below employee costs, and Claude licence spend is more than offset by benefits.

qa_highlights.question: Are layoffs happening due to AI efficiency?
qa_highlights.answer: No layoffs; leavers are not being replaced unless exceptional, and hiring is on a requirement basis.

qa_highlights.question: Threat from larger players chasing smaller deals?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said large players cannot economically serve small niche deals (for example, Big Data), so no material threat is seen.

qa_highlights.question: Deal pipeline size and five-year plan?
qa_highlights.answer: About USD 1 million of pipeline; management plans new verticals in cybersecurity and SAP, and a possible small acquisition within five years, with no current plan.

risks_watch: Revenue softness for two to three quarters as ramp-downs flow through; covering the two lost clients' revenue expected to be slow.
Concentration: top 10 clients are over half of revenue, and two large-client losses hit this quarter.
Middle East pipeline is empty for the next few quarters; growth relies on Europe, Australia and the US.
Token/AI tooling costs rising as a share of cost base; margin impact not quantified.
Monitor Q2 FY27 for revenue trend and whether the USD 300K and USD 250K deals and the bank AI project convert.
Revenue guidance withdrawn; FY28 guidance deferred to March 2027.
summary.management_tone: Cautious on revenue and explicitly conservative ("I do not want to give any false hope"), while confident on margins and AI-driven productivity. Management was candid about the two client losses but leaned on qualitative claims (pipeline, AI wins) that were not quantified.
key_quotes: I would like to be conservative. I do not want to give any false hope.
we are now moving one step forward, and we are already two steps back.
The developer efficiency, I would say, is almost 25%, so what four people were doing earlier is now being done by almost two people, at a very high level.
I have approximately 1 million US dollars of pipeline at this moment.

financial_highlights.change: +389 bps YoY (26.4% in Q1 FY26); vs 29.3% in Q4 FY26
vs Rs 2.71 in Q1 FY26 (+43% YoY)

growth.why: FY27 revenue guidance cut and withdrawn: growth now capped at 4-5% (flat-ish at midpoint ~2.5%), with softer revenue expected for 2-3 quarters as ramp-downs flow through; no capacity additions, backing is vague (AI productivity and a pipeline of ~USD 1m), and the 25-30% EBITDA margin target was held.
